name: engram-tools

tools.name: engram_start
tools.description:
Begin meaningful work in a repository with a Markdown briefing: session id, ranked private/public memory, workspace guidance and optional checklists. Unlike engram_smarter, this includes workspace onboarding/activation guidance; unlike engram_rehydrate, it prepares a starting briefing instead of reconstructing a prior journal. Use once when beginning work; choose engram_smarter for a task switch and engram_rehydrate for recovery.

Supply repo and task when known; context overrides the generated project/market/role/stack/task query. Reuses one eligible active journal; new_session=true deliberately creates a separate journal. Supply session_id for parallel work. Ambiguous automatic selection returns 409; list sessions and choose an exact id. Records a session event; repeating may add events or open another session. Consumes workspace daily call quota; quota exhaustion requires reset or a plan change, not immediate retries. OAuth: memory:read and session:write.

session_id.description: Exact journal id from start/rehydrate/list_sessions. Disambiguates parallel work; writing requires your active session. Rehydrate may read shared or closed history.

agent_tool.description: Calling client name for attribution, e.g. codex, claude-code, cursor, or gemini. Omit if unknown.

project.description: Product/project name for session context. Start/setup use it as the repository hint when repo is omitted.

repo.description: Repository slug, e.g. engram or billing-api, within the authenticated workspace. This is a memory filter, not a filesystem path or workspace selector.

role.description: Agent responsibility used in task context, e.g. backend engineer. Start/setup default to implementation agent.

market.description: Business/domain context, e.g. fintech or education; not a geographic access setting.

task.description: Concrete current goal or decision, e.g. diagnose checkout retries; used to focus context and session recovery.

stack.description: Project technologies used to focus context; omit when unknown.

items.description: Technology name, e.g. TypeScript or PostgreSQL.

context.description: Optional full task context; overrides the query generated from project, role, market, stack and task.

new_session.description: Default false reuses one eligible active journal. True creates a separate journal for parallel work; retries can create another session. Keep the returned session_id.

include_skills.description: Include relevant procedural checklists. If omitted, the server infers this from task/context keywords; false suppresses checklists.

limit.description: Maximum retrieved memories, 1–30. Omitted defaults: focused=8, deep=16; explicit values override these defaults.

depth.description: Default focused uses a small retrieval budget; deep expands it when focused results are insufficient. An explicit limit overrides the default budget.

tools.name: engram_rehydrate
tools.description:
Recover interrupted work after compaction, resume or lost context. Returns Markdown checkpoints, decisions, gotchas, open loops and recent events. Unlike engram_start, this restores the prior journal when available; unlike engram_recall or engram_smarter, it recovers session history rather than only searching durable knowledge.

session_id selects an accessible workspace session. Closed or teammate journals are read-only history, never reopened. Automatic recovery requires one active journal for this member, repo/project and authenticated OAuth connection or supplied agent_tool within the recovery window. Multiple matches return 409: list sessions and choose an id. since filters events after selection. If none matches, loads durable task memory and opens a journal. Repeating active recovery adds events; it does not erase history. Consumes workspace daily call quota. OAuth: memory:read and session:write.

session_id.description: Exact journal id from start/rehydrate/list_sessions. Disambiguates parallel work; writing requires your active session. Rehydrate may read shared or closed history.

agent_tool.description: Calling client name for attribution, e.g. codex, claude-code, cursor, or gemini. Omit if unknown.

project.description: Product/project name for session context. Start/setup use it as the repository hint when repo is omitted.

repo.description: Repository slug, e.g. engram or billing-api, within the authenticated workspace. This is a memory filter, not a filesystem path or workspace selector.

task.description: Concrete current goal or decision, e.g. diagnose checkout retries; used to focus context and session recovery.

reason.description: Recovery trigger, e.g. context compaction or resumed after interruption; recorded in the journal.

depth.description: Default standard: up to 30 events/4 summaries; brief uses 12/2, full 60/8. This controls journal detail, not retrieval depth.

since.description: Optional ISO 8601 lower bound for journal events, e.g. 2026-10-16T10:00:00Z; omit for normal recent-session recovery.

tools.name: engram_recall
tools.description:
Answer one concrete question from authenticated workspace/public memory before deciding or debugging. Unlike engram_smarter, this retrieves question-specific evidence without task checklists; unlike engram_get_context, it returns one ranked memory list instead of separate category samples. Use engram_rehydrate to recover an interrupted session.

Returns JSON with ranked memories, ids, trust/conflict signals and retrieval hints. Example: {"repo":"engram","query":"What did we learn about Netlify SSR costs?"}. No matches returns count=0; deepen or rephrase rather than assume the answer. repo/type/tags narrow the question; limit overrides the depth budget. Records retrieval telemetry without editing knowledge. Consumes workspace daily call quota; stop on quota errors and retry only transient failures. OAuth: memory:read.

query.description: Specific decision, error or question to search, e.g. how are checkout retries deduplicated?

repo.description: Repository slug, e.g. engram or billing-api, within the authenticated workspace. This is a memory filter, not a filesystem path or workspace selector.

type.description: Knowledge category: team rule, reusable pattern, pitfall, proven fix, design decision, or library/version quirk.

tags.description: Topic labels for storing or filtering memory; omit when no useful labels apply.

items.description: Searchable topic label, e.g. oauth or postgres.

session_id.description: Exact journal id from start/rehydrate/list_sessions. Disambiguates parallel work; writing requires your active session. Rehydrate may read shared or closed history.

limit.description: Maximum retrieved memories, 1–20. Omitted defaults: focused=5, deep=12; explicit values override these defaults.

depth.description: Default focused uses a small retrieval budget; deep expands it when focused results are insufficient. An explicit limit overrides the default budget.

tools.name: engram_store
tools.description:
Save one durable lesson privately for future workspace agents; returns a confirmation. Use engram_reflect for a milestone with several lessons/outcomes and engram_report_outcome to assess an existing memory.

To correct knowledge, supply the complete replacement in content and old ids in supersedes_memory_ids; change_reason explains the replacement. Old entries retain history; this is not permanent deletion. Similar content may deduplicate and boost confidence, so retries can have effects. Consumes memory/call quota; rejects secrets and low-quality content. OAuth: memory:write.

type.description: Knowledge category: team rule, reusable pattern, pitfall, proven fix, design decision, or library/version quirk.

content.description: One durable, self-contained lesson, up to 20,000 characters. State the decision/fix and why it matters; exclude secrets and transient debug logs.

repo.description: Repository slug, e.g. engram or billing-api, within the authenticated workspace. This is a memory filter, not a filesystem path or workspace selector.

tags.description: Topic labels for storing or filtering memory; omit when no useful labels apply.

items.description: Searchable topic label, e.g. oauth or postgres.

agent_tool.description: Calling client name for attribution, e.g. codex, claude-code, cursor, or gemini. Omit if unknown.

session_id.description: Exact journal id from start/rehydrate/list_sessions. Disambiguates parallel work; writing requires your active session. Rehydrate may read shared or closed history.

context.description: Non-sensitive supporting metadata, e.g. {language: "typescript", component: "auth"}; never credentials or raw customer data.

supersedes_memory_ids.description: Up to 20 accessible memory ids explicitly replaced by this lesson; omit for an ordinary new memory. Old entries retain their history.

items.description: Exact id from a recalled memory; do not substitute a repository name, URL, or the memory text.

change_reason.description: Why the supplied memories are superseded, up to 1,000 characters; used with supersedes_memory_ids.

tools.name: engram_report_outcome
tools.description:
Record whether a recalled memory helped; returns a confirmation. Use its exact memory_id and evidence in detail. success=false may include failure_reason; outdated marks obsolete knowledge, while success raises confidence.

Only accessible workspace/public memories may be reported. Repeating adds outcomes and changes confidence; do not blindly retry. Use engram_store with supersedes_memory_ids for a verified replacement, or engram_reflect to batch milestone outcomes. Consumes workspace daily call quota. OAuth: outcome:write.

memory_id.description: Exact id from a recalled memory; do not substitute a repository name, URL, or the memory text.

success.description: Whether this memory helped the actual task: true for a useful application, false for a misleading or unusable result.

detail.description: Brief evidence of how the memory changed the decision, or why it failed. Exclude secrets.

failure_reason.description: Why an unsuccessful memory failed; outdated marks obsolete knowledge. Omit for a successful use.

repo.description: Repository slug, e.g. engram or billing-api, within the authenticated workspace. This is a memory filter, not a filesystem path or workspace selector.

session_id.description: Session where this memory was retrieved; used for outcome attribution, not to reopen or modify that journal. May be closed.

tools.name: engram_cross_pollinate
tools.description:
Reuse a lesson solved in another repository before rebuilding a shared pattern. Unlike engram_recall or engram_smarter, this explicitly excludes target_repo from source searches and adds transfer lessons and quality gates. Returns Markdown with ranked memories and source repos from other authenticated workspace repositories, with optional public knowledge.

source_repos restricts the search; include_public supplements sparse private results. Records retrieval telemetry without copying knowledge. Consumes workspace daily call quota. OAuth: memory:read.

target_repo.description: Destination repository slug for the current work; memories from this repo are excluded from the source search.

context.description: Natural-language task and relevant facts, e.g. migrate our PostgreSQL schema with zero downtime. Never include credentials or raw customer data.

session_id.description: Exact journal id from start/rehydrate/list_sessions. Disambiguates parallel work; writing requires your active session. Rehydrate may read shared or closed history.

source_repos.description: Restrict source repositories to these slugs; omit or pass an empty array to search other repositories.

items.description: Source repository slug in this workspace.

include_public.description: Default true: supplement private results with public knowledge when needed. False searches only other private workspace repositories.

limit.description: Maximum retrieved memories, 1–25. Omitted defaults: focused=5, deep=12; explicit values override these defaults.

depth.description: Default focused uses a small retrieval budget; deep expands it when focused results are insufficient. An explicit limit overrides the default budget.

tools.name: engram_smarter
tools.description:
Brief a materially different task within the same session. Unlike engram_recall, this combines goal-focused memories with optional procedural checklists; unlike engram_get_context, it ranks evidence for the task instead of returning category samples. Returns Markdown with ranked workspace/public memory and retrieval hints. Use engram_start to begin work and engram_rehydrate for lost context.

Example: {"repo":"engram","context":"Improve public-page delivery on Netlify while preserving localized SEO and onboarding."}. context states the whole goal; repo/file focus retrieval without reading local files. limit overrides depth; include_skills=false suppresses checklists. Records retrieval/session telemetry without editing knowledge. Consumes workspace daily call quota. OAuth: memory:read.

context.description: Natural-language task and relevant facts, e.g. migrate our PostgreSQL schema with zero downtime. Never include credentials or raw customer data.

repo.description: Repository slug, e.g. engram or billing-api, within the authenticated workspace. This is a memory filter, not a filesystem path or workspace selector.

file.description: File path/name used only as a search hint, e.g. src/auth.ts. Engram does not read or modify local files.

include_skills.description: Include relevant procedural checklists. If omitted, the server infers this from task/context keywords; false suppresses checklists.

session_id.description: Exact journal id from start/rehydrate/list_sessions. Disambiguates parallel work; writing requires your active session. Rehydrate may read shared or closed history.

limit.description: Maximum retrieved memories, 1–30. Omitted defaults: focused=5, deep=12; explicit values override these defaults.

depth.description: Default focused uses a small retrieval budget; deep expands it when focused results are insufficient. An explicit limit overrides the default budget.

tools.name: engram_reflect
tools.description:
Checkpoint a milestone or handoff for later recovery with engram_rehydrate. Supply at least one of summary, learnings, used_memories or feedback. Returns Markdown with stored/skipped counts, outcomes and next actions. Use engram_store for one lesson and engram_report_outcome for one outcome.

store=false skips learning storage only: the journal and supplied outcomes/feedback can still be written. This checkpoint leaves the session open. Retrying may duplicate writes; verify prior success first. Consumes workspace daily call quota and memory quota for saved lessons. OAuth: session:write, memory:write and outcome:write.

repo.description: Repository slug, e.g. engram or billing-api, within the authenticated workspace. This is a memory filter, not a filesystem path or workspace selector.

task.description: Concrete current goal or decision, e.g. diagnose checkout retries; used to focus context and session recovery.

session_id.description: Exact journal id from start/rehydrate/list_sessions. Disambiguates parallel work; writing requires your active session. Rehydrate may read shared or closed history.

summary.description: Milestone/handoff summary: what changed, evidence, decisions and remaining work. Required unless learnings, outcomes or feedback are supplied.

agent_tool.description: Calling client name for attribution, e.g. codex, claude-code, cursor, or gemini. Omit if unknown.

store.description: Default true saves accepted durable learnings; false skips learning storage only. Session checkpoints, supplied outcomes and feedback are still recorded.

used_memories.description: Outcomes for memories actually used during this milestone; only the first 20 are processed. Omit when none were applied.

memory_id.description: Exact id from a recalled memory; do not substitute a repository name, URL, or the memory text.

success.description: Whether this memory helped the actual task: true for a useful application, false for a misleading or unusable result.

detail.description: Brief evidence of how the memory changed the decision, or why it failed. Exclude secrets.

failure_reason.description: Why an unsuccessful memory failed; outdated marks obsolete knowledge. Omit for a successful use.

learnings.description: Durable private workspace lessons to persist when store=true; only the first 8 are processed. Low-quality entries may be skipped. The summary remains a journal checkpoint.

type.description: Knowledge category: team rule, reusable pattern, pitfall, proven fix, design decision, or library/version quirk.

content.description: One durable, self-contained lesson, up to 20,000 characters. State the decision/fix and why it matters; exclude secrets and transient debug logs.

tags.description: Topic labels for storing or filtering memory; omit when no useful labels apply.

items.description: Searchable topic label, e.g. oauth or postgres.

context.description: Non-sensitive supporting metadata, e.g. {language: "typescript", component: "auth"}; never credentials or raw customer data.

feedback.description: Optional product feedback or feedback-pulse dismissal; separate from outcomes about individual memories.

signal.description: Quality of Engram retrieval during this work; omit if only dismissing the feedback pulse.

notes.description: Concrete non-sensitive feedback explaining the selected signal.

dismiss.description: True permanently dismisses the optional weekly feedback pulse for this agent member.

tools.name: engram_skill
tools.description:
Find a procedural checklist before a repeatable task. Omit skill or pass an empty string to list available names; otherwise load a name such as code-review or skill:code-review.

Returns JSON with available_skills/usage for listing or skill/count/steps/combined for a guide. Unknown names return count=0 and a message. Reads workspace/public knowledge without installing or executing anything. Use engram_recall for a project fact and engram_smarter for task-based guide selection. Consumes workspace daily call quota. OAuth: memory:read.

skill.description: Checklist name, e.g. code-review, security or skill:deployment. Omit or pass an empty string to list available names; unknown names return count=0.

tools.name: engram_get_context
tools.description:
Audit repository knowledge by category: conventions, gotchas, patterns, solutions and architecture. Unlike engram_recall or engram_smarter, this searches each category separately and returns five sample arrays for coverage review, rather than one task-ranked list. Returns JSON with repo/file/total and up to 21 entries; this is a bounded search, not a full repository-memory export.

repo is required; file/task refine search without reading files. Only when all five categories have no repo matches does the search broaden to workspace/public memory. Empty results are valid. Does not edit knowledge. Consumes workspace daily call quota. OAuth: memory:read.

repo.description: Repository slug to inspect, e.g. billing-api. If no repo-specific memories match, the server broadens to workspace/public knowledge.

file.description: File path/name used only as a search hint, e.g. src/auth.ts. Engram does not read or modify local files.

task.description: Concrete current goal or decision, e.g. diagnose checkout retries; used to focus context and session recovery.

tools.name: engram_setup
tools.description:
Explain onboarding and inspect the authenticated workspace when an agent needs setup guidance. Returns one JSON response with plan/counts/limits, tool groups, activation checklist and suggested calls; no pagination or installation.

Hints personalize examples: project names the work; repo scopes activation guidance, falling back to project when omitted. Does not configure the machine, open a working session or edit knowledge. Use engram_start to begin work, engram_rehydrate to recover it and engram_proof to audit adoption. Consumes workspace daily call quota; exhaustion requires reset or a plan change. OAuth: memory:read.

agent_tool.description: Calling client name for attribution, e.g. codex, claude-code, cursor, or gemini. Omit if unknown.

project.description: Product/project name for session context. Start/setup use it as the repository hint when repo is omitted.

repo.description: Repository slug, e.g. engram or billing-api, within the authenticated workspace. This is a memory filter, not a filesystem path or workspace selector.

role.description: Agent responsibility used in task context, e.g. backend engineer. Start/setup default to implementation agent.

market.description: Business/domain context, e.g. fintech or education; not a geographic access setting.

task.description: Concrete current goal or decision, e.g. diagnose checkout retries; used to focus context and session recovery.

stack.description: Project technologies used to focus context; omit when unknown.

items.description: Technology name, e.g. TypeScript or PostgreSQL.

tools.name: engram_proof
tools.description:
Audit adoption before a rollout or when checking whether the workspace is using memory and reporting outcomes. Takes no arguments. Returns JSON with memory-bank breakdowns, learning-loop activity, proof points and a benchmark checklist.

Does not change knowledge or run a benchmark. Use engram_setup for onboarding and engram_recall for task knowledge. Consumes workspace daily call quota. OAuth: memory:read.

tools.name: engram_list_sessions
tools.description:
Find an exact session_id before recovery, closing or a handoff. Unlike engram_rehydrate, this lists bounded metadata without replaying journal content or changing a session. Returns JSON sessions with member/client attribution, status, activity and checkpoint availability, plus next_cursor.

Default scope=mine lists this member's sessions; scope=workspace explicitly includes teammates in the authenticated workspace. repo/status/agent_tool/member_id filter results; a teammate member_id requires workspace scope. limit defaults to 20, maximum 50. Pass next_cursor unchanged to continue newest-started-first pagination. Empty results are valid. Consumes daily call quota. OAuth: memory:read.

repo.description: Repository slug, e.g. engram or billing-api, within the authenticated workspace. This is a memory filter, not a filesystem path or workspace selector.

scope.description: Default mine lists your sessions across clients; workspace includes shared teammate session metadata.

status.description: Filter journal state; omit to include both active and closed sessions.

agent_tool.description: Calling client name for attribution, e.g. codex, claude-code, cursor, or gemini. Omit if unknown.

member_id.description: Member id to filter; another member requires scope=workspace. This is a filter, not authorization.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the prior response. Keep filters unchanged; omit for the first page.

tools.name: engram_close_session
tools.description:
Finish an exact journal at a real completion or handoff. Unlike engram_reflect, this atomically closes the session after saving a supplied final summary or confirming an existing checkpoint. Durable memories and journal history remain; closure ends journal writes without erasing knowledge. Returns JSON with session_id, closed_at, checkpoint_id, already_closed and memories_retained.

Get session_id from start/rehydrate/list_sessions. Only this session's member or a human workspace owner may close it; team read access does not grant close authority. A missing checkpoint or failed save leaves it active. Repeating close returns the original receipt without duplicate summaries. Closed journals are read-only for explicit rehydrate and cannot be implicitly reopened. Consumes daily call quota. OAuth: session:write.

session_id.description: Exact journal id to close; required. Never pass a repo slug or a natural-language query.

summary.description: Final checkpoint text, at most 6000 characters and no credentials. Omit when reusing an existing checkpoint. Erased journals reject new text; omit to reuse their redacted checkpoint, or start a new session.

tools.name: engram_retract_memory
tools.description:
Withdraw an exact private memory that should no longer guide agents. Unlike engram_store with supersedes_memory_ids, this needs no replacement and keeps the content for explicit restoration. Unlike engram_delete_memory, it is reversible. Returns JSON memory_id, RETRACTED status and already_retracted.

Get memory_id from recall/context; provide a non-sensitive reason, 1–1000 characters. Only the creator or a human workspace OWNER may withdraw it; team read access is not write authority. Current retrieval excludes it and source-dependent patterns. Recovery suppresses free text in referencing journals rather than replay withdrawn guidance. Start a clean session for new work or restore the source. Repeating is idempotent. Public-bank and superseded records are excluded. Consumes daily call quota. OAuth: memory:write.

memory_id.description: Exact id from a recalled memory; do not substitute a repository name, URL, or the memory text.

reason.description: Why this knowledge should stop guiding agents, 1–1000 characters. No secrets or copied sensitive content.

tools.name: engram_restore_memory
tools.description:
Make an explicitly retracted private memory available again. Unlike engram_store, this restores the original ID/content; storing matching retired content returns 409 rather than silently reviving it. Returns JSON memory_id, ACTIVE status and already_active. Retained source-dependent history becomes available when no other withdrawn sources remain.

Only the creator or a human workspace OWNER may restore. Memory quota still applies. A confirmed replacement or SUPERSEDED state requires the separate replacement-review workflow; permanently erased IDs cannot be restored. An already active record is an idempotent no-op. Consumes daily call quota. OAuth: memory:write.

memory_id.description: Exact id from a recalled memory; do not substitute a repository name, URL, or the memory text.

tools.name: engram_delete_memory
tools.description:
Preview or permanently erase one private memory and its explicit derived patterns from the live database. Unlike engram_retract_memory, execution cannot be undone. Requires a human workspace OWNER API key; OAuth agents and member keys cannot erase. Does not delete independent memories or unrelated sessions.

Default dry_run=true returns counts, derived IDs, affected session IDs (first 50), scope and confirmation. Inspect it first: execution redacts the entire free-text history/checkpoints/task/context of referencing sessions, plus associated outcomes, links, jobs and linked evidence; shared entities remain if still referenced. Execute only the reviewed ID using dry_run=false and confirmation="delete:<memory_id>". Returns erased_at/counts; repeated execution returns the original minimal ID/count receipt without erased text (a one-way content fingerprint blocks exact store replays). In-flight background writes and exact store retries cannot repopulate erased knowledge. Historical unlinked paraphrases, already delivered client context, application/provider logs, provider copies and backups are outside this live-database operation. Public-bank records are excluded. Consumes daily call quota.

memory_id.description: Exact id from a recalled memory; do not substitute a repository name, URL, or the memory text.

dry_run.description: Default true previews impact without changing knowledge. False executes only with the exact confirmation string and human OWNER authority.

confirmation.description: For execution only: copy delete:<exact memory_id> from the preview. Omit for preview; never substitute a repo name.

instructions:
Engram is shared workspace memory, available across repositories. Call engram_start at the beginning of meaningful work in each repository, with the current repo and task. Infer repo from the active project, never from the folder where Engram was installed. After compaction or resume, call engram_rehydrate before continuing. Recall before non-trivial decisions, store only durable non-sensitive lessons, report outcomes for memories used, and reflect at milestones. Follow the nearest project Engram contract when present. Never store credentials, secrets, or raw customer data.

Choose retrieval by intent: engram_recall answers one question; engram_smarter briefs a new task in the same session; engram_get_context audits memory by category. Use engram_cross_pollinate when another repository is likely to have a reusable lesson. For parallel work, pass the returned session_id to journal-writing calls; use engram_list_sessions when the target is ambiguous. engram_reflect leaves the session open; optionally use engram_close_session at a real finish or handoff. Closing keeps durable memories and history.

Tools share the workspace's plan-dependent daily call quota, resetting at midnight UTC. On a quota error, wait for reset or ask the owner to review the plan; repeated calls consume quota without resolving the limit. Correct invalid arguments or missing OAuth scopes before retrying. Refresh expired OAuth credentials; a temporary connection failure alone does not require reauthorization. Read tools can be retried after transient failures, but start, rehydrate, store, report_outcome and reflect can write: check whether a prior call succeeded before repeating it.
